extracted.intended_audience: mathematics researchers (prospective authors and reviewers) and journal subscribers/librarians
extracted.subtask_short: submitting to Pacific Journal of Mathematics
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and policies for authors preparing and submitting mathematical research manuscripts to the Pacific Journal of Mathematics, and for reviewers handling submissions under the journal's editorial procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aims and scope — high-quality mathematical research
rubrics_metrics.description: The Pacific Journal of Mathematics 'has published high-quality mathematical research in a broad range of mathematical subjects since 1951.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions should be research articles in mathematics suitable for a broad range of mathematical subjects; the journal emphasizes high quality and long-standing publication of mathematical research. The journal publishes articles at low cost to libraries and individuals and provides authors with a rigorous and professional editorial process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics and policies — editorial principles and author obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: Information about the journal's editorial principles, its policies for authors, the handling of complaints and appeals, and copyright and licensing can be found in the journal's ethics and policies documentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors are expected to follow the journal's ethics and policies (including copyright/licensing rules and complaint/appeal procedures). Specific details and obligations are provided in the linked ethics and policies pages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer-review process — single-anonymized review
rubrics_metrics.description: This journal operates a single-anonymized review process (the names of the reviewers are hidden from the author).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Further information, including expectations and responsibilities for the journal and for reviewers, is available on the peer-review process page. Authors and reviewers should follow the single-anonymized conventions described there.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication schedule — frequency and page budget
rubrics_metrics.description: The Pacific Journal of Mathematics publishes 12 issues per year, for an expected total of about 2400 pages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should be aware of the journal's publication frequency and approximate annual page capacity when considering submission timing; editorial scheduling operates within this framework.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access model and embargo — subscription with delayed open access
rubrics_metrics.description: Access to the journal is by subscription. All articles become free to access and read six years past publication (meaning on the sixth January 1st after the publication date).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should note that, unless otherwise arranged (see Subscribe to Open), articles are behind subscription for an initial period and become free after the stated six-year embargo.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author fees — no charges to authors
rubrics_metrics.description: The journal does not charge any author fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors will not be required to pay publication fees to PJM under the stated policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subscribe to Open — contingent open-access model
rubrics_metrics.description: PJM adopted the Subscribe to Open model: each year, if enough subscribers continue to support the journal, that year's articles will be published open access — free to read by everyone and with no author charges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should consult the Subscribe to Open documentation for details. The page notes that, thanks to subscribers, all 2023–2026 articles in PJM are published open access; prior recent articles may still be subscription-only.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preservation of access — CLOCKSS and LOCKSS membership
rubrics_metrics.description: To ensure the long-term availability of our published online content, MSP is a member of CLOCKSS and of the Global LOCKSS Network.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This assures authors that published content is preserved in recognized digital preservation networks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission format — PDF submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors may submit manuscripts in PDF format via the provided submission link.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manuscripts should be prepared and submitted as PDF files. Authors must use the submission portal linked on the page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow submission guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should follow the journal's submission guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed instructions (Formatting, length expectations, bibliographic style, figure handling, supplemental material, etc.) are provided in the linked submission guidelines; authors should consult and comply with those specifics before submitting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publisher and editorial stewardship — MSP practices
rubrics_metrics.description: The journal is published by MSP (Mathematical Sciences Publishers), a nonprofit that offers low-cost, scholar-led journals and provides a rigorous editorial process; MSP developed EditFlow, the peer-review web application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors and reviewers can expect MSP's standard editorial infrastructure and policies; MSP frames itself as a nonprofit steward of quality and fairness in journal publishing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indexing and journal metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: PJM is indexed in MathSciNet (American Mathematical Society), zbMATH Open (FIZ Karlsruhe), Scopus (Elsevier), and Scimago Journal Rank; it is also listed in Web of Science and Journal Citation Report / Impact Factor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors may cite indexing and metrics when assessing journal visibility; the presence in these services is part of the journal's quality/visibility considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact and production information
rubrics_metrics.description: Contact information is provided for editorial matters (Barbara Pawley: pacific@math.ucla.edu), production matters (Silvio Levy: production+pjm@msp.org), and subscriptions (subscriptions+pjm@msp.org), plus mailing addresses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors and others should use these contacts for editorial queries, production questions, or subscription matters; specific contacts are listed for appropriate types of inquiries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Journal metadata and bibliographic information
rubrics_metrics.description: Metadata given: first published 1951; size/periodicity: 12 issues per year; ISSN 1945-5844 (online) and 0030-8730 (print); physical dimensions listed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This bibliographic metadata should be used when preparing citations, submissions, or requests to the journal.
